artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta \subset \mathbb{C}$ be an open disc with origin $0$, and let $\Delta^* = \Delta \setminus \{0\}$. Let $f \colon Y \to \Delta$ be a proper holomorphic map with $Y$ a smooth complex manifold, such that the restriction $f \colon f^{-1}(\Delta^*) \to \Delta^*$ is a smooth proper submersion with connected fibers. Denote the singular fiber by $V_{s_0} = f^{-1}(0)$ and a nearby smooth fiber by $V_s = f^{-1}(s)$ for $s \in \Delta^*$. The Picard–Lefschetz monodromy associated to a loop around $0$ acts on $H^q(V_s, \mathbb{C})$; transporting to the special fiber via the specialization map, one obtains an endomorphism $T \colon H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C}) \to H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C})$.

Call a class $\psi \in H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C})$ a local invariant cohomology class if $T(\psi) = \psi$.

Question: For every integer $q \geq 0$ and every local invariant cohomology class $\psi \in H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C})$, does there exist a class $\widetilde{\psi} \in H^q(Y, \mathbb{C})$ whose restriction to $V_{s_0}$ equals $\psi$? Equivalently, is the restriction map $H^q(Y, \mathbb{C}) \to H^q(V_{s_0}, \mathbb{C})^T$ surjective?
artifact.status_search_result: The local invariant cycle conjecture (originally posed by Griffiths) was proved over the complex numbers. Clemens–Schmid established it via limit mixed Hodge structures; Deligne gave an independent proof using the Weil conjectures (in the algebraic setting), and it also follows from the BBDG decomposition theorem. The theorem is now standard and goes by the name "local invariant cycle theorem".

status_evidence.title: Local invariant cycle theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectured by Griffiths in 1970 and proved by Clemens and Schmid; a different proof by Deligne.

status_evidence.title: Sur le théorème local des cycles invariants (Deligne)
status_evidence.snippet: Deligne's proof of the local invariant cycle theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Deligne provided a proof of the theorem.

status_evidence.title: The Decomposition Theorem and the Topology of Algebraic Maps
status_evidence.snippet: The local invariant cycle theorem is a direct consequence of the decomposition theorem of BBDG.
status_evidence.claim: It also follows from the decomposition theorem.
